citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
An enclosure housing 20 pigeons is not being cleaned frequently enough, leading to an accumulation of excreta. There
are elevated wooden surfaces in the enclosure with accumulations of dried excreta on them. There are also two plastic
pet travel crates in the enclosure that have excreta on the tops and along the protruding rims.
An accumulation of feces and excreta can lead to increased disease hazards or illnesses, attract pests, and create odors.
Excreta and food waste must be removed from primary enclosures and from under and around primary enclosures as
often as necessary to prevent an excessive accumulation of feces and food waste, to prevent soiling of the birds
contained in the primary enclosures, and to reduce disease hazards, insects, pests, and odors.
The facility cleaned the enclosure at the time of the inspection.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
